items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: I called Walter Barnes that had a band... and I knew him and I called him, and he set me up in Chicago

ctx.x: Now, Eddie South had been begging him to join him, a hundred and fifty dollars a week and lodging, doing nothing but playing the white hotels; he says he told him no, I'm with Ernie Fields band, but if you're all going back to Oklahoma, I'm going to tell him I'll accept it. He said now, if any other dates come on, you make up your mind, I'm with you as long as you're here, I'm not going to let you down, but

when you head back, I'm going on with South.
Anyway, I told the guys I'd see
and I got to make a little contact around and
then I talked it over with Willard. He said I
think you shouldn't go back, Fields, but I know
how you feel and it would be a little weight
off me, but he said we have representatives in
that area and they can do something, but I'll
tell you what, you went over really good down
in Philly and if you know you're going to go
back, he called a man--I don't remember him now,
but he said I think he…

on the whole group, all but one person, was burning in the fire in Mississippi, and I knew him and I called him, and I had been getting some very good press write ups in the paper and he set me up in Chicago and I played Chicago and I think booked a date in Wichita, Kansas. And, as I told you, Rozelle, when we headed--if I remember right, Rozelle went to Philly with us and after then he told us he'd bid us goodby.
